definition: In this historical source, sensory consciousness means the conscious side of sensory stimulation or sensory change. It is used in the idea of mental dynamogenesis, where a change in sensory consciousness tends to be followed by a change in motor consciousness.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Dynamogenesis; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not support the claim that “sensory consciousness means the conscious side of sensory stimulation or sensory change.” It only uses the phrase “change in sensory consciousness” within the discussion of “mental dynamogenesis,” without defining what “sensory consciousness” specifically means.

The remainder (“…used in the idea of mental dynamogenesis, where a change in sensory consciousness tends to be followed by a change in motor consciousness”) is supported in the packet, but the definition’s first sentence is not.
